# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 2 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 2

---

*[The speech of the ungodly: verses 1–20]*

**2:1** For they reasoned falsely among themselves, saying: "Short and sorrowful is our life, and there is no remedy at a man's end, and no one has ever been known to return from Hades.

**2:2** For we were born by mere chance, and afterward we shall be as though we had never existed; because the breath in our nostrils is smoke, and reason is a spark struck from the motion of our hearts,

**2:3** which once extinguished, the body will turn to ashes and the spirit will dissolve like empty air.

**2:4** Our name will be forgotten in the course of time, and no one will recall our deeds; our life will pass away like the fading traces of a cloud, and will disperse like a mist driven before the sun's rays and overcome by its heat.

**2:5** For our time is the passing of a shadow, and our end admits no postponement; it is sealed, and no one reverses it.

**2:6** Come then, let us enjoy the good things that are present, and make full use of creation with the eagerness of youth.

**2:7** Let us fill ourselves with costly wine and perfumes, and let no flower of spring pass us by.

**2:8** Let us crown ourselves with rosebuds before they wither.

**2:9** Let none of us miss his share of our festivity; everywhere let us leave tokens of rejoicing, for this is our portion and this is our lot.

**2:10** Let us oppress the righteous poor man; let us not spare the widow, nor show regard for the grey hair of the aged.

**2:11** But let our strength be our standard of righteousness; for what is weak is by that fact found to be useless.

**2:12** Let us lie in wait for the righteous man, for he is an inconvenience to us and opposes our works, reproaching us for violations of the law and charging us with offenses against our upbringing.

**2:13** He claims to have knowledge of God, and calls himself a child of the Lord.

**2:14** He has become a living reproach to our way of thinking; he is a burden to us even to look upon,

**2:15** because his manner of life differs from all others, and his ways are entirely strange.

**2:16** He regards us as base metal and avoids our ways as unclean; he counts the end of the righteous as blessed, and boasts that God is his father.

**2:17** Let us put his words to the test, and find out what will happen at the end of his life.

**2:18** For if the righteous man is the son of God, God will take up his cause and will rescue him from the hand of his opponents.

**2:19** Let us subject him to humiliation and torment, so that we may learn how gentle he really is and put his patience to the proof.

**2:20** Let us condemn him to a degrading death, for according to his own argument he will be looked after."

**2:21** Such were their thoughts — but they were mistaken; their wickedness had blinded them,

**2:22** and they did not know the hidden purposes of God, nor did they hope for the reward of holiness, nor did they discern the honor reserved for blameless souls.

**2:23** For God created the human person for imperishability, and made him in the image of his own eternity;

**2:24** but through the envy of the devil, death entered the world, and those who belong to his side experience it.

---

## Council Notes

**On v. 1 — "reasoned falsely":** LOGOS and SOPHIA adopt "reasoned falsely" over EMET's "not rightly." The Greek ou orthōs means "incorrectly" but in a context that implies deliberate distortion. PNEUMA's colloquial "got it completely wrong" (placed at v. 21) is excellent but too informal for the opening frame.

**On v. 11 — "standard of righteousness" vs. "law of righteousness":** All agents discussed. EMET's "law" is literal (nomos) but the ungodly are precisely rejecting law; "standard" (LOGOS) captures that they have substituted might-as-criterion for law-as-criterion.

**On v. 13 — "child of the Lord" vs. "servant of the Lord":** pais kyriou is the key ambiguity. EMET and PNEUMA render "child"; LOGOS offers "servant." SOPHIA adopts "child of the Lord" — this is the ungodly's mockery of his claim to divine sonship, and the term anticipates the Suffering Servant typology without collapsing it.

**On v. 23 — "imperishability" vs. "incorruption":** EMET uses "incorruption"; LOGOS and PNEUMA use "imperishability." SOPHIA adopts "imperishability" (aphtharsia) as the philosophical register of this text demands a term that signals ontological status, not merely moral purity.

**On v. 24 — "those who belong to his side":** EMET "those who belong to his portion"; LOGOS "those who belong to his side"; PNEUMA "those who take the devil's side." SOPHIA adopts LOGOS's "those who belong to his side" as cleanest.
